analysis.title: TSMC: Potential collaboration with Tesla for US fab – JPM thoughts
key_insights: Elon Musk indicated over the weekend that TSLA / SPCX is in discussions with TSMC for US semiconductor capacity. This follows news last week that TSMC will consider building a second US Fab Cluster in Texas. Nothing has been finalized.

JPM supply chain checks indicate early discussions aim at a pure Foundry relationship or a JV (similar to JSMC or ESMC) that would give TSLA/SPCX a dedicated capacity corridor. The fab is expected to ramp in 2030 and beyond.
The first three phases of TSMC's US expansion are likely to still focus on Arizona. US fab capacity has been a key impediment to expanded Foundry engagement between Tesla and TSMC.

JPM expects TSMC to keep control of process and technology and to run fab operations. It is unlikely to agree to technology sharing, unlike the Intel-Tesla TeraFab agreement on the 14A process. Co-investment is possible, but JPM would be surprised if TSMC did not own a majority of the fab.
JPM sees strong compute demand as the primary driver. SPCX has been able to sell compute at $20-30 per watt, which implies significant ROIC on compute sales and urgency to add capacity.

JPM has picked up signals of slower progress on a competitor's process ramp (Tesla AI6 may be re-engaging with TSMC). New ASIC programs, likely with Mediatek, are also on TSMC process rather than Intel.
TSMC appears more open to building capacity at an accelerated pace given strong compute demand and a desire not to become the primary bottleneck for customers.
JPM maintains OW on TSMC with a Jun-27 PT of NT$3300 (20x 12m forward EPS). The potential Tesla cooperation points to a diminished competitive narrative, which could support TSMC's P/E multiple.
A larger switch-back to TSMC by TSLA could benefit GUC, the current design partner for AI5, which had faced the prospect of share loss on AI6.

Thesis: AI demand for leading-edge wafers stays strong, with capacity expansion in N3 and N2 and an earlier ramp of A14. A14 is expected to enter mass production in 1H28, with some revenue in 2H28. Tight leading-edge supply is expected to extend into 2027-28.

JPM expects gross margins to stay in the mid-high 60% range, with N2 dilution offset by strong N3 demand, 1H27 price hikes and cross-fab collaboration. Margins could approach 70% once N2 dilution becomes modest, likely late 2027 or early 2028.

market_movers.rationale: Potential Tesla/SPCX US fab collaboration diminishes the competitive narrative and could support the P/E multiple. Price was NT$2575 on 05 Oct 26.
GUC (3443.TW), the AI5 design partner, could benefit if TSLA switches back to TSMC more broadly, after facing possible share loss on AI6. Price NT$8,600, OW.

sector_views.rationale: Tight leading-edge wafer supply is expected to extend into 2027-28, driven by AI demand and accelerated capacity builds.

earnings_insights: JPM expects TSMC gross margins to stay in the mid-high 60% range (forecast), with a chance of approaching 70% in late 2027 or early 2028 as N2 dilution fades.
JPM's PT of NT$3300 is based on about 20x 12-month forward P/E (forecast basis), above TSMC's five-year average multiple.
risk_factors: Debate on the duration of the AI capex growth cycle.
geopolitical: TSMC is considering a second US Fab Cluster in Texas, with the first three phases of US expansion still focused on Arizona.

key_data_points.context: About 20x 12m forward EPS, above the five-year average multiple. Raised from NT$3,200 on 17-Jul-26, then NT$3,300 on 30-Sep-26.
